articleTitle: Electric Load Forecasting Using Multiple Output Gaussian Processes and Multiple Kernel Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Electric load forecasting refers to forecasting the electricity demand at aggregated levels. Utilities use the predictions of this technique to keep a balance between electricity generation and consumption at each time and make accurate decision for power system planning, operations, and maintenance, etc. Based on prediction time horizon, electric load forecasting is classified to very short-term, short-term, medium-term, and long-term. In this paper, a multiple output Gaussian processes with multiple kernel learning is proposed to predict short-term electric load forecasting (predicting 24 load values for the next day) based on load, temperature, and dew point values of previous days. Mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) is used as a measure of prediction accuracy. By comparing MAPE values of the proposed method with the persistence method, it can been seen that the proposed method improves the persistence method MAPE up to 4%.

articleTitle: YOLOv5-M: A Deep Neural Network for Medical Object Detection in Real-time
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: COVID-19 pandemic is still a global health issue, causing about 684 million cases and 6.84 million deaths around the world. Personal protective equipment (PPE) such as gloves, face masks, face shields, goggles, etc., can be an effective measure to combat COVID-19. In this work, we proposed, YOLOv5-M, a modified version of YOLOv5, for medical object (PPE and face mask) detection tasks. Experiment results on a recent five-class real-time, challenging dataset CPPE-5 (medical PPE) show the effectiveness of YOLOv5-M. YOLOv5-M outperformed four other existing state-of-the-art object detectors: Faster-RCNN, Single shot object detectors, YOLOv3, and YOLOv5 in terms of training speed, and model performance. The proposed model is also tested on the Face mask detection dataset, and it achieves competitive performance. Apart from that, maintaining proper social distancing inside hospitals among healthcare workers and patients is critical in minimizing nosocomial transmission. Despite the commodity of PPE, some individuals may still get infected with COVID- 19. The proposed system also has the feature of calculating the social distance between healthcare workers. Taken together, the proposed system has the potential to be implemented in real-time healthcare settings.

articleTitle: Automating Conference Paper Assignment Using Classification Algorithms Incorporated with TF-IDF Vectorisation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Assign submitted papers to the right topics or reviewers with the right expertise in a research conference is important. However, the paper assignment process is presently a repetitive and time-consuming manual task. This study aims to automate the process by building a classification model incorporating TF-IDF vectorisation. We outline a data mining methodology consisting of data selection, text pre-processing, transformation, classification, evaluation, and optimisation. A data set of 1,000 conference papers with five research topics was carefully selected, pre-processed, and transformed into a TF-IDF vector representation. The TF-IDF vector was then applied to six popular document classification algorithms: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Naïve Bayes (NB), Logistic Regression (LR), K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN), Decision Tree (DT) and Random Forest (RF). Initially, these algorithms with default parameters were evaluated and measured using F-measure. Then, the top three among them were further optimised using Grid Search. The results revealed SVM as the best-performing algorithm, with an F-measure score of 0.907.

articleTitle: Hardware Requirements for 2D Cylindrical-High Pass Ladder Coil Design enabling Homogeneous Excitation in Ultra High-Field MRI
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: This paper discusses the hardware architecture of a volumetric 2D c-HPL radio frequency MRI coil. Five prototypes using different inductor-capacitor (LC) resonator combinations are constructed. The experimentally obtained eigenfrequencies are compared with those obtained theoretically from the dispersion equation. The transverse and longitudinal coupling coefficients are approximately 6% and 9%, respectively. An individual element consisting of 12 pF capacitors at each end and a simple tunable non-magnetic variable capacitor resulted in a single-element resonance frequency. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex>, of 286 MHz. For a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\ \mathrm{x}\ 6$</tex> array with this individual resonance, the experimentally obtained, coupled, eigenfrequencies were measured as 274.17 MHz, 276.98 MHz, 280.2 MHz, 283.82 MHz, 286.63 MHz, 296.68 MHz (imaging mode), and 305 MHz, which is in good agreement with the dispersion equation.

articleTitle: Sustainable Energy-Based Voice-Controlled Home Automation Using IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Home automation has become an integral part of our daily lives and has evolved since our inception to bring feasibility and compatibility to our homes and workplaces. The basic foundation of home automation is the ability to control lights, fans, kitchen utensils, etc., automatically. Google Home, Amazon Echo, and Apple Home Kit are the most widely used home automation systems. This document will build a voice-enabled home automation project that is both efficient and cost-effective. Using WI-FI and IOT, it can be remotely controlled and monitored using an Android device. We use sustainable energy to power microcontrollers to minimize costs and build environmentally friendly projects. Ordinary home appliances are used to implement the system. The Google Assistant receives natural language voice commands, which are converted and sent to the microcontroller via the IFTTT (If This Then That) and Blynk applications. The microcontroller then controls the relays that are connected as needed and turns the devices connected to each relay on or off in response to a request from the user to Google Assistant. For connection between the microcontroller and the application (Internet), a Node-MCU (ESP8266), including a Wi-Fi module, is used. Using sustainable energy in this project restores the energy supply, eliminates carbon dioxide emissions and maximizes energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study on the Impact of GIC on Pipe-to-Soil Potential of Buried Pipeline Near Equatorial Region
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Geomagnetic induced current (GIC) is an aftermath effect of space weather activity that caused disruption to earth-related applications including the Impressed Current Cathodic Protection System (ICCP), a corrosion mitigation system of buried pipelines. ICCP performance degrades by large voltage swings caused by GIC, thus corroding the pipeline faster. The effect of GIC on the ICCP system had been investigated in high-latitude regions, however, fewer discoveries on this subject matter in Equatorial Region particularly near the geomagnetic equator. This paper presents the effect of GIC based on the H component of the Earth's magnetic field with the Pipe to Soil Potential (PSP), during moderate and intense geomagnetic storm events day. Results show that the H component variations and its time derivative had a stronger relationship during intense geomagnetic storm events. This study also found a new finding, i.e., the PSP was also out of the safe range with the possible effect of equatorial electrojet (EEJ), a daily variation of the H component. This has made the PSP swing out of the safe range even during moderate geomagnetic storm days. This research is important in understanding the cause and extent of the impact of GIC in the process of controlling pipeline corrosion where safety issues may arise in the long run due to this event.

articleTitle: Video Analysis to Detect Dress Code Violations in Laboratories
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: The rapid advancement of image and video processing technology has led to a significant increase in its application. Particularly during the global COVID-19 pandemic, the automated analysis of camera footage has gained paramount importance in the automatic detection of events. This includes identifying violations or suspicious occurrences to ensure safety, such as the detection of mask or personal protective equipment (PPE) usage in controlled areas. Aligned with this context, the objective of this study is to develop a real-time video analysis system for object detection, specifically focusing on monitoring compliance with dress codes in laboratory settings. The system utilizes a combination of pretrained YOLOv3, Caffe, and custom-trained Mobilenet models to identify individuals who are not wearing face masks or lab coats. The custom Mobilenet models were trained using two datasets, achieving an accuracy rate of 0.81 for face mask detection and 0.92 for lab coat detection, surpassing the minimum objective of 0.80 for both categories. These promising results underline the potential of this approach in significantly enhancing safety within laboratory environments.

articleTitle: Application of Reinforcement Learning to UR10 Positioning for Prioritized Multi-Step Inspection in NVIDIA Omniverse
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Sequential multi-step operations have long played an important role in manufacturing systems. In high level multi-step manufacturing processes, multiple operations are carried out in sequence on different machines/robots, while in low level applications, multi-step operations are performed by a single robot. This paper in particular studies the multi-step inspection problem with focus on robot-positioning. Traditionally, multi-step robot positioning was implemented in engineering cycles under a set of predetermined conditions. Nonetheless, due to recent trends towards mass-customization, the dynamic nature of working environments coupled with uncertainty has imposed multi-step robot positioning tasks with challenges that transcend static engineering cycles and require an automated adaptation process when dealing new products. Based on the requirements associated with multi-step inspection processes (in the context of mass-customization), and the associated dynamicity and uncertainty, this paper investigates the use of reinforcement learning in bringing automation into the development of inspection systems by focusing on the multi-step robot positioning problem. The simulations have been implemented for a set of state of the art reinforcement learning algorithm including DDPG, TD3, TRPO and PPO via NVIDIA Omniverse, Isaac Sim environment. Our experiments indicated that TRPO demonstrated the overall best performance for the accuracy in visiting the inspection points and job rejection rate, whereas PPO, as a theoretically more capable method, exhibited a lower performance.

articleTitle: Design Half Bridge DC-DC LCC Series-Parallel Loaded Resonant Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: This paper presents the designing of Half-Bridge DC-DC LCC Series Parallel Loaded Resonant Converter. The objectives of these analysis are to investigate the function of the loaded resonant converter and generate low voltage supply for application electronic devices. Series parallel resonant converter (SPRC) is combination of parallel resonant converter (PRC) and series resonant converter (SRC), thus taking their benefits and eliminating their disadvantages. The value that need to be determined in the design of the converter is inductance and capacitance in the resonant tank, desired output voltage and current. The 20 kHz switching frequency and zero voltage switching technique are used in the design of this converter to efficiently generate output. This converter performs a voltage output of LCC in the resonant tank before the output voltage and the current generate the load. The converter design is simulated and investigated using PSIM simulation software. The result is recorded to examine the converter's operation and concept.

Author Keywords: Series Parallel Resonant Converter (SPRC) Inductor Capacitor Capacitor (LCC)

articleTitle: Leveraging Robust CNN Architectures for Real-Time Object Recognition from Conveyor Belt
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: In the contemporary era, the problem of recognizing undesirable objects and individuals on the conveyor belt is addressed by various architectural or algorithmic approaches. Conveyor belts are an object-carrying medium by which things go in a straight line for transportation. However, sometimes some unwanted objects go through the belt mistakenly, which can be very dangerous. Hence, detection accuracy is much needed to avoid such deadly occurrences and better accuracy can be achieved by performing detection in real time. Furthermore, this upgraded system will assist individuals by lowering the danger of any accidents and provide a real-time example of an airport conveyor belt by detecting any unwanted moving objects with the help of different algorithms and methods of the neural network. Therefore, in this paper, we offer a few algorithms that comprise Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), YOLOv5, YOLOv7, and Vision Transformer (ViT) as well as some Transfer learning methods over a few pre-trained models (VGG16, ResNet50, MobileNetV2) to produce a better strategy on our customized dataset to find out if it can recognize objects and human babies. Our research indicates that our custom dataset closely fits the architecture of YOLOv5, with an accuracy of 88%.

articleTitle: Detection and Mitigation of SQL and Jamming Attacks on Switched Beam Antenna in V2V Networks Using Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: This research article proposes a federated learning approach for detecting and mitigating SQL injection and jamming attacks on switched beam antenna in V2V networks. The proposed approach utilizes the collective intelligence of multiple nodes in the network to train a machine learning model for detecting malicious traffic patterns. We evaluate the performance of the proposed approach using both simulated and real-world V2V network data, and demonstrate its effectiveness in improving network security and performance. Our results show that the proposed approach can significantly reduce the latency and throughput overhead associated with conventional security mechanisms, while maintaining high levels of accuracy in detecting attacks.

articleTitle: Design of Load-Dependent Dual-Mode 12V to 5V Step-Down Voltage Regulator for MCU-CPU Powered Wireless Sensor System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: A power management unit to power a hybrid CPU wireless sensor system is first designed and simulated using LTSpice. Multiple operation modes and adaptive loading are simulated and studied. Transient response under various modes are measured, with best-worst undershoot of 0.183V-1V and best-worst overshoot of 0.184V-0.283V. Power efficiency is 94% at 3A maximum loading current and peak power efficiency is 96.2% at 1.5A loading current. The final PCB is constructed using freeware tools KiCAD.

articleTitle: Enhancing Physicochemical and Dielectric Properties of Palm Oil-Natural Fiber Blends Through Varying Preparation Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of preparation methods on the electrical and chemical properties of palm oil-natural fiber blends. Refined, bleached, and deodorized palm oil (RBDPO) is used and mixed with rice husk (RH) that has been refined and sieved to 63 micrometers. Two types of samples with the same concentration are prepared. The first sample is prepared by first stabilizing the temperature of the hot RBDPO to room temperature before it is mixed with RH and sonicated. The second sample is prepared where RH is immediately mixed with the hot RBDPO and is not sonicated. The breakdown voltage (BDV) test is performed following the guidelines specified in IEC 60156, using the Megger OTS100AF oil tester. The obtained data is subsequently analyzed using the Weibull statistical method to evaluate the distribution of the BDV in the sample. The dielectric response at various frequencies is examined over a range of 102 -105 Hz. The moisture-absorbing characteristics of RH in the mixture are assessed using Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. A notable enhancement in both the mean BDV and dielectric permittivity of the second sample was observed. Data analysis shows that this could be due to moisture absorbing properties of RH in the mixture of the second sample is superior.

articleTitle: Implementation Tool Machine Learning Features Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: In recent trends, machine learning in EDA tool features is a hotcake. It covers floorplanning, placement optimization, congestion optimization, routing optimization, as well as design space optimization with artificial intelligence capability. With machine learning capability, the design is expected to converge faster with a higher quality of result in timing, power, and routing utilization. This paper will review the current artificial intelligent state of the arts, in chip design optimization. The paper will discuss the type of artificial model deployed in the field as well as the preferred model in the field. The evaluation is done on commercially supported artificial intelligent features in the EDA tool, at various implementation stages, including stability tests of the commercial artificial intelligent features. From the finding, machine learning does improves the predictability of quality of result however, there is a need for forward looking controller to ensure the optimum quality of result from combined machine learning features. Hopefully, the finding of existing artificial intelligent features supported and limitations will benefit the design community.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network Object Detection Algorithm for Identifying Species of Panthera
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Panthera is a genus in the Felidae (cat) family that includes three well-known species: i) tigers, ii) lions, and iii) jaguars. This genus is also known as “big cats”. Panthera is also considered the most dangerous and extinct animal. It is very important to protect the Panthera species. However, it is challenging to identify the species as they share some similarities in characteristics such as the shape of the face, size, etc. Therefore, an artificial intelligence approach is used to solve this problem. The goals of this project are to design and develop a system that can detect three Panthera species automatically: 1) tiger, 2) lion, and 3) jaguar. The system is developed with a Convolutional Neural Network algorithm and the methodology of the project is using the Waterfall model. There are four phases in the Waterfall model i) requirement analysis, ii) system design, iii) implementation, and iv) testing. The results show that the deep learning model can achieve accuracy of 100% in the training set and 93.33% in the testing set.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a GCash Cash-in and Cash-out Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: The increasing number of GCash users in the Philippines comes with demands for available machines for cash-in and cash-out transactions. However, cash-in machines are only available as of the moment, while cash-out through kiosks and remittance centers are overwhelmed with long queues. This paper presents a method of design and development of a machine that is able to do GCash cash-in and cash-out transactions. It is composed primarily of bill acceptor, touch screen monitor, microcontroller, computer unit, and coin hopper and vacuum system for dispensing bills. The machine is tested and evaluated based on its functionality and acceptability. Each of the components were tested for 17 different amounts in Philippine peso. As a result, all of the devices are 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> functional. The speed of transaction for each cash-in and cash-out transaction is tested three times for each bill in Philippine peso (P): 20, 50, 100, 500, 1000. In result, the average speed for cash-in transaction is 31.16s for all bills mentioned while for cash-out, an average of 30.22s for bills P20, P50, and P100, and 44s for P500 and P100 bills. These transaction speeds are reasonable enough for GCash credit transfer transactions. In the future this machine will be further developed with added features, faster, and efficient devices integrated to it.

articleTitle: Three-level DC-DC Buck Converter Architecture Using Digital Pulse Width Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: This study demonstrates a high efficiency 3-level DC-DC buck converter using DPWM (digital pulse width modulation). It is mainly featured with the replacement of traditional flying capacitor with a capacitive voltage divider, which will constantly maintain the half of the supply input voltage. Consequently, one of the power MOSFETs in the output stage will be removed to reduce conversion loss. The duty cycle is found to be as high as 93.75<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> and the peak efficiency is 98% at 6.25 MHz switching clock rate by all-PVT-corner simulation.

articleTitle: AI Based Automated Food Recognition Using CNN for Fitness Mobile Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Eating a healthy, balanced diet with regular exercise is important for maintaining physical and mental health. Healthy diet and exercise promise a healthier lifestyle. Other than that, people competing in different sports need a customized, strict workout and diet plan. Trainees offer their best at gymnasium by following a strict workout plan recommended by their coaches. However, there is no way till now to determine if the trainees are taking the prescribed diet strictly. Therefore, an optimized application with the feature of real time scanning of the prescribed meal can be helpful to overcome this problem. For this purpose, we have used Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) along with Image Processing. Using ResNet50 with activation functions of ReLU and Softmax, our trained CNN model and the proposed architecture achieved an accuracy of 82.70 percent. We used CNN pre-trained models such as InceptionV3 with LeakyReLU and Softmax, InceptionV3 with ReLU and Softmax, VGG16 with ReLU and Softmax, VGG16 with ReLU and Softmax, and ResNet50 with ReLU and Softmax, so the achieved accuracy, respectively, is 78%, 71%, 58%, 56%, and 82.7%. Therefore, the proposed model has the potential to achieve high performance on real time food scanning which can be used in online fitness platforms(mobile applications and websites) and fitness gadgets.

articleTitle: Expense Tracking with Tesseract Optical Character Recognition v5: A Mobile Application Development
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Tracking daily expenditures is fundamental to managing personal finances. There are many ways to track personal expenditures. The common but inconvenient ways are manually recording expenses using paper and pen or note-taking applications on mobile phones. Thus, this preliminary study aims to develop a convenient Expense Tracking Mobile Application to track users” daily expenses and visualise their spending data using charts and statistics. Users can extract expenses from receipts using Tesseract Optical Character Recognition (OCR) version 5, which implements Long Short-term Memory (LSTM). The mobile application was evaluated using 20 receipts from grocery stores and markets. The result showed that the average Character Error Rate (CER) and Word Error Rate (WER) for items in receipts were 9.36%, and 19.39%, respectively. At the same time, the average CER and WER for unit prices in receipts were 2.26% and 4.33%, respectively. The mobile application was also evaluated using the System Usability Scale (SUS) and obtained a satisfactory score of 71.5%.

articleTitle: Characterization of Heterostructure Capacitive Humidity Sensor Using Indirect Capacitance to Voltage Converter Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Fruits can easily become soggy and rot when exposed to a humid environment. Therefore, fruit needs to be placed at a suitable humidity level and maintained at that level from time to time to prevent fruit damage. This paper designs a capacitive humidity sensor with a 281-sensitivity value of a heterostructure composed of hematite and nickel oxide as sensing materials connected to an indirect capacitance to voltage converter circuit, which is a combination of an astable multivibrator circuit and a Zener-regulated frequency to capacitance converter used as a detector circuit with 2.41 mV/%RH sensitivity to determine the humidity level (%). Variations in capacitance values cause variations in the output voltage that can be justified by the amount of water vapor present in fruit packaging. The sensing method is based on the fundamental principle of capacitance changes, which are produced by the interaction of water vapor with sensing material.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition on Partial Faces with Histogram of Oriented Gradients and Local Binary Patterns
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Facial expression is a way to improve the ability of communication. If machines can understand the emotion, their responses should be improved. Many researchers can teach the machine to learn emotions from facial images. Sometimes, the face in an image may not be complete, especially when the masks are used in pandemic. Some parts of the human face cannot be reached. However, if the important features can be extracted from the remaining parts, the machine should be able to learn. In this paper, Histogram of Oriented Gradient (HOG) and Local Binary Pattern (LBP) are considered to extract features from the upper-frontal facial images. The concatenation of these features is also studied. The experimental results show the combined features provide the most stability performance with the highest averaged accuracy at 68.39% on Support Vector Machine.

articleTitle: Weigh-in-Motion Implementation Along North-South Expressway Malaysia
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Premature damage to roadways caused by overweight vehicles increase hazards to road users, slow down traffic, increase lane shutdowns and increase road maintenance costs. To minimize premature pavement damage along the North-South Expressway (NSE) between Thailand and Singapore, weigh-in-motion (WIM) systems have been installed to measure vehicle-in-motion weight based on a combined information capture of speed, axle count and weight detected by piezoelectric sensors within the expressway pavement. Preliminary results from WIM systems deployed at 13 locations along the NSE and 6 more at NSE interconnections indicate that 3 - 16% of Heavy Vehicles in general along the NSE are overloaded. At WIM locations adjacent to Singapore and Thai borders, 13.8 - 16% of Heavy Vehicles traveling were detected as overloaded. With such data from WIM system monitoring confirming significant overloading, what remains is how best to notify, divert, police and impose suitable deterrent penalties effectively with an ideal result of penalties recouped to pay for premature expressway damage. Also presented in this paper is an overview of existing WIM system implementation, present and future challenges faced, and potential solutions.

articleTitle: IOT-Enabled Vacuum Cleaner Using Arduino
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: The objective of this study is to develop an IOT-enabled automatic vacuum cleaner using Arduino that can be controlled by using smartphone. This vacuum robot is capable of cleaning the entire floor of homes, rooms, and offices. In this project, Arduino Mega is used as the microcontroller. Additionally, this robot is equipped with HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensors that can detect walls, obstacles, and cliffs. When there are obstacles in front of the robot, its movement will be modified according to the Arduino Mega algorithm. Using these sensors, a path planning algorithm was developed to enable the robot to move and efficiently clean the entire room. With the addition of a wireless ESP8266 receiver module, the robot can be controlled wirelessly via a smartphone running the Blynk application. The user can choose between two modes of automatic cleaning, or they can control it manually. Therefore, this provides a wireless control even when the user is not at home so long as they are connected to wi-fi, and it can also be controlled automatically without the assistance of others.

articleTitle: FOUNDATION™ Fieldbus Cascade Control in the Field Tuning Using Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Control in the field (control strategies used in fieldbus field devices) provides increased flexibility and cost efficiency, as well as improved process integrity in industrial plant operations. Despite the benefits listed above, communication delays caused by FOUNDATION™ the most typical issues encountered while adopting fieldbus technology are fieldbus networks and control loops. Using particle swarm optimization, this work proposes an effective tuning solution for cascade control strategies implemented in fieldbus field devices. The proposed optimal tuning approach is compared to the Ziegler-Nichols tuning method using a level-flow cascade control plant model in the Delt V distributed control system. Furthermore, experimental results showed that the proposed tuning strategy improved control loop performance.

articleTitle: Lotus - An Undergraduate Capstone Design Project Framework for Environmental Monitoring Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: A prototype of a semi-autonomous robotic system, called Lotus, has been developed to collect field sensor data in the Salton Sea region of the Imperial Valley. The system is constructed using commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) components and is powered by an 8-bit MCU and a 64-bit CPU. Power management techniques, including energy harvesting and charge control, as well as adaptive load control, have been adopted. A long-range wireless communication radio with a custom-designed antenna is also included. In order to reduce data transmission, image recognition utilizing TensorFlow's machine learning algorithm is employed. This project serves as a capstone project essential for ABET accreditation and establishes a framework for a continuous improvement process aimed at promoting awareness and proposing solutions to address a local environmental problem.

articleTitle: Soft Transition Scheme of Sensorless Controlled IPMSM for EV Compressor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel soft starting and transition control scheme of IPMSM to suppress the speed ripple and acoustic noise. The open-loop started IPMSM has to be transferred to a closed-loop sensorless control scheme at the base speed region. The conventional linear current decreasing to synchronize the open-loop angle to the estimated rotor position can be easy implemented. However, the linear current decreasing makes torque variation and speed ripple at the transition point. In the proposed method, the synchronization function is determined by the square of position error between the open-loop angle and the estimated rotor position. According to the load condition, the torque angle can be fast move to the MTPA(Maximum Torque per Ampere) point at the starting point of synchronization region. And it is slowly changed around of MTPA point due to the reduced position error. The fast moving but the soft transition can be implemented with reduced torque ripple and speed ripple at the transition in the proposed method. Furthermore, the speed controlled open-loop starting method can reduce the speed variation from the standstill to transition speed region. Unlike the conventional I/F method, the open-loop torque reference is defined by the open-loop speed reference and speed error together to reduce the mechanical vibration from the non-linear disturbance at the starting. The proposed soft starting and transition control scheme is verified by the practical IPMSM(Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor) for EV(Electric Vehicle) compressor driving. In the compared experimental results, the proposed method shows the improved open-loop starting and transition performance.

articleTitle: RSSI Power Detector for Drone Charging Using Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles having different equipment such as cameras, sensors etc. have their range and flying time limited due to their battery capacity. Researchers are looking into ways of charging the battery using a wireless power transfer system. Received signal strength indicator function then becomes a very crucial requirement for such a system as it will not only detect the strength of the wireless power transfer signals but will also alert the drone of the location where these signals are maximum. This paper presents a 0.3 - 6 GHz power detector based on reverse - RSSI architecture that can detect +50 dBm of input power to be used for drone charging application. A resistor-based-attenuation array with five stages of asymmetrical source - coupled full wave CMOS rectifiers are used in the design that provides a dynamic range of around 48 dB occupying a core area of 0.009 mm2. The proposed architecture uses a thick gate oxide transistor to enable it to detect high power in a standard CMOS process. RSSI system designed in this paper is intended to be used for charging of drones, mid-air, using WPT system coupled with antenna array.

articleTitle: A Single-Switch Bidirectional AC Chopper-Based Electronic Load Controller for Pico Hydropower System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: This paper proposed a simple electronic load controller (ELCr) for a pico hydropower system. The electronic load controller is used to regulate the output power of hydropower generators, thereby maintaining the output voltage and frequency at desired values. Conventionally, the diode bridge rectifier with IGBT ELCr is used in pico hydropower. However, it injects harmonics into the system. The phase regulation technique also suffers from harmonics and is limited by the timing accuracy of the trigger pulse. Hence a single-switch bidirectional AC chopper (SSBAC) - based ELCr is proposed. This SSBAC ELCr uses a single IGBT per phase to switch voltage and current bi-directionally to the dump load. From the simulation studies, the SSBAC ELCr produced excellent voltage regulation with low order harmonics at a value of 3.21%. The SSBAC ELCr maintained the generator's torque constant and provided a balanced distribution of power in each phase.

articleTitle: Fin Configuration Affects under Natural Convection Heat Transfer for Rectangular Fin Heatsink Using Steady-State Thermal Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Heatsinks are significant to IC devices as they prevent the chip from overheating. The present study investigates different configurations of rectangular fin heat sinks. Autodesk Fusion 360 is used to design a finite element modelling-based to study the effects of different configurations of the rectangular heat sink design with aluminium and copper materials. The modified configurations of the rectangular fin heat sink, which are in-line and staggered, were studied under natural convection heat transfer. These models were analyzed using different mesh conditions by varying the element size for each fin configuration. Using Ansys Workbench, the steady-state thermal analysis was observed based on the maximum temperature and total heat flux under various heat loads (8 W, 12 W and 24 W). The simulation shows that finer-size elements gave a stable result in the total heat flux but did not show a significant difference in the maximum junction temperature. The in-line fin configuration with copper material showed the lowest maximum junction temperature. The result was consistent at all heat loads. Furthermore, the in-line fin configuration also gave the highest total heat flux among other configurations at all heat loads for both copper and aluminium materials. The conducted studies can be used as initial findings to achieve an optimum design based on fin configurations and predict the heat flow parameters in a rectangular fin heatsink.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of IoT Mobile Edge Computing Networks Using a DF/AF UAV-Enabled Relay with Downlink NOMA
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: This work investigates a system for non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)- mobile edge computing (MEC) in the Internet of Things (IoT) using an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) as a relay. We investigate a scenario in which an edge cluster of IoT devices (IDs) with limited resources is unable to compute their own tasks and must instead offload them to two MEC access points (APs) via the UAV relay (UR). As a result, we propose a five-phase procedure to ensure NOMA-based task offloading. We derive closed-form formulas for the successful computation probability (SCP) under the Rayleigh fading channel model to evaluate the system's efficacy. The numerical results show how major system parameters such as average transmit power, number of ID, and UR height affect the results. The Monte-Carlo simulation validated the precision of our investigation.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Cloud based Dashboard for Indoor Vertical Farming System using ThingsSentral
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: The ever-increasing population of the world has created more demand for food and the conventional agricultural system is struggling to meet this demand. The vertical farming system is a novel method of farming compared to the traditional agricultural system that has proven to be a sustainable system for food production. Integration of Internet of Things (loT) technology with vertical farming system has enhanced the efficiency of yield generation by allowing the user to monitor the farm's environmental conditions and status in real time, ensuring minimum loss. A cloud platform is essential for hosting and visualizing the vertical farm's data in real time. In this research, ThingsSentral cloud platform has been chosen for hosting and visualizing the developed vertical farming system's environmental data. An ESP32 based control system has been developed that reads the sensors' values, controls the water and light, and transmits the sensor values to the cloud platform. ThingsSentral Cloud has been chosen due to the flexible and versatile features offered by this cloud platform.

articleTitle: BeeNow - A Remote Beehive Monitor using IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Beekeeping is a time intensive and laborious task, especially in the realm of commercial beekeeping. In his paper, the design and building of prototype model of a remote beehive monitor that a beekeeper could use to more efficiently manage a hive and garner useful data on the hive's health is discussed. The main goal was to track their weight and temperature over time. Additionally, orientation was important to track in case the hives were pushed over or moved without the beekeeper's knowledge. Finally, to further assist the beekeeper, the remotely feed the hives and automate the process without the beekeeper needing to be on site is discussed. The design methodology of the hardware and system is explained. The results obtained and future directions for more accurate automation of the system is also discussed.

articleTitle: Educational Data Mining: A Systematic Review on the Applications of Classical Methods and Deep Learning Until 2022
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Educational Data Mining (EDM) is a research field that focuses on extracting valuable insights and knowledge from data in the education sector. EDM exploits Data Mining (DM) techniques such as Clustering, Regression to analyze data and make predictions that help answer questions in education. Meanwhile, Deep Learning (DL) is a subfield of machine learning that uses neural networks to solve complex problems related to natural language processing and computer vision. DL is highly effective at processing textual and digital data such as images, audio, and video. DL can be applied to build automatic grading, attendance, monitoring systems, or intelligent learning systems in education. However, the applicability of DL in education still needs to be solved due to strict education regulations and policies with the many challenges involved in collecting and utilizing data processes. Additionally, education is subject to many ethical and legal controversies. This survey aims to clarify the concepts and issues related to EDM, such as technology, users, and data. It also explores the technologies and applications of DL in the educational environment, including the barriers and difficulties encountered when applying these technologies. Finally, the survey offers some comments on the future development direction of this field.

articleTitle: Factors Influencing Customers Intention to Use Digital Banking Services
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: This study aims to evaluate the factors influencing customers” intention to use digital banking services. The main theoretical framework is based on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM)., extended with social image and perceived self-efficacy. This study is able to gather data from 230 respondents using online surveys., which are then subjected to structural equation modeling (SEM) analysis in SMART PLS. The result shows that attitude toward using and perceived self-efficacy are the main drivers of customers” intention to use digital banking. In contrast., perceived usefulness is found to have no significant impact on intention to use. Perceived usefulness., perceived ease of use., and social image are found to positively impact attitude toward using. Lastly., perceived usefulness is found to be influenced by perceived ease of use. Despite its limitations., this study contributes academically to the technology acceptance research through the extension of TAM in the digital banking context and provides managerial insights for future digital banking development in Indonesia.

articleTitle: The Role of Social Media on Purchase Decisions in Indonesia: Perspective of Z Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: The technological revolution had a significant impact on people's lifestyles. With the development of technology, more and more social media are being created. Social media that is now widely used, namely Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, Twitter, etc. is one indication of the increasing use of the internet and people's need for online shopping. Currently, almost all social media have implemented live streaming and even shop features, which can increase usage and consumption rates, especially for Generation Z. Generation Z has an open way of thinking and likes instant things, including shopping. Apart from the convenience provided by social media, various impacts help Generation Z in making purchasing decisions. Therefore, this research was conducted to find out whether the role of social media can help Generation Z in making purchasing decisions, with the risks that exist in social media. With a sample of 300 respondents including Generation Z, who make purchasing decisions online, this research was collected through a quantitative survey method. The results of the questionnaire data will be analyzed using IBM SPSS version 28, while the model and structural measurements are analyzed using SmartPLS 4. The results of data collection show that Generation Z, in making purchasing decisions, does not care about the risks involved. Perceived risks are considered insignificant, but the theory holds that it is significant to consumers. Therefore, future research should consider whether the role of social media use in Generation Z has a different risk perception.

articleTitle: Similarity Measures for Person Identification with Face Mask
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Facial recognition is a method of identifying or verifying a person's identification by examining their face. People can be identified in pictures, videos, or in real time using facial recognition technology. After facing more than two years of Covid-19 restrictions, face masks are optional but strongly advised for usage. As new cases are still recorded on a daily basis, wearing face mask in a social setting is still the safest way to protect ourselves and others from COVID-19. However, the usage of face mask has brought difficulties for a person or face identity recognition because half of the face features has been covered. The proposed research starts with face mask detection for determining if the subject is wearing a mask or not. The system uses MobileNetV2 for face mask detection resulted to 100% correct when identifying face mask. Secondly, to evaluate the effectiveness of various similarity coefficient formula for person identification with face mask. A dataset of 35 people wearing face masks was examined. The study involving usage of multiple similarity measures formula; Euclidean Distance, Cosine Similarity, Manhattan Distance, and Jaccard Similarity to evaluate the similarity between two images. It is identified that Jaccard Similarity is the most sensible similarity coefficient method for person identification with face mask. This study offers some insight that worth to further analyses the potential of Jaccard coefficient in measuring the person identity with a face mask.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Comparison Highly Efficient Active Rectifier for Energy Harvesting Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: A piezoelectric energy harvesting (PEH) circuit with a passive rectifier lack in efficiency and performance. The performance and potential of piezoelectric energy-harvesting devices depend strongly on the power conditioning circuit as the circuits are essential for managing and controlling energy flows in these energy collecting devices. In order to overcome this situation, the parallel synchronized switch harvesting on inductor (P-SSHI) and the general model of synchronized multiple bias-flip (SMBF) which are the recent implementation of parallel synchronized triple bias-flip (P-S3BF) and parallel synchronized septuple bias-flip (P-S7BF) are used for further enhancing the PEH performance. In addition, active rectifiers presented distinguished benefits over passive rectifiers, such as the ability to analyze regulation, dynamic response to load changes, output voltage ripple, input current, total harmonic distortion (THD), power factor correction, and wave factor. Furthermore, by using an active rectifier the output voltage can be boosted higher. Thus, it is more efficient than a lower voltage since it experiences less energy loss from resistance. This research investigates the several high efficiency AC-DC active rectifiers as interface circuit plays a crucial role in the energy harvesting capability enhancement in PEH systems. The research methodology is carried out on a piezoelectric structure under the same base circuit with a different type of power conditioning circuit applied to the main circuit using the LTspice software. In conclusion, the input voltage for each different active rectifier circuit were set at 3–5 V and the frequency is set based on the input voltage of the circuit. Based on the results, the P-S7BF shows the higher efficiency with voltage output will have the most efficiency with the estimated voltage output reaching up to 13 V with a net harvesting power of up to 80-90% follow up by the P-S3BF and P-SSHI. There are several recommendations to improve active circuit by investigation the impact of load variation on the efficiency, such as different loads may require different rectification techniques and control strategies to achieve high efficiency.

articleTitle: Hashtag Recommendation based on Neural Topic Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Hashtag recommendation for microblogs is an appealing research topic that can assist users in selecting hashtags for their microblogs. Previous hashtag recommendations have been proposed based on the topic model approach. In spite of their improvement, two issues are still unresolved. First, prior studies inferred the topic distribution of users, words, and hashtags by using a non-neural network framework, making them unable to deal with the complex topic distribution of users, words, and hashtags. Second, previous work required word and hashtag frequency to process the topic distribution inference only, ignoring not only word ordering and word context but also the relation between word and hashtag. It is one of the crucial factors that affect hashtag recommendation since some words in the target microblog can indicate the relevant hashtags. In this paper, we propose a novel hashtag recommendation model called Hashtag-NTM to infer the topic distribution of users, words, and hashtags by using the neural network framework, making the model able to deal with the complexity of distribution. Moreover, we explore the relationship between words and hashtags to model word and hashtag representation before processing topic distribution inference, making the recommended hashtags more related to words in the target microblog. Extensive experiments on the Twitter dataset demonstrate that Hashtag-NTM consistently outperforms baseline methods over hit rate metrics.

articleTitle: Ultraviolet Disinfection for Bio-Contaminated Surfaces with Image-Based Navigation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Transmission of Covid-19 the virus had brought massive efforts regarding the delay and stopping of the process of virus transmission. Disinfection is one of the techniques to stop disease transmission among people. Ultraviolet disinfection is one of the solutions for stopping and delaying the virus transmission process through bio-contaminated air and surfaces. Therefore, this paper presents to develop a UV sanitization robot with multifunction uses and low costs based on Wireless Sensor Technologies. This UV robot model design is controlled by a microcontroller and interfaced with mobile apps such as Blynk. This UV disinfection robot's designed function is to disinfect the surrounding. Additional features had been added to this robot design such as monitoring the process of disinfection, obstacle detection, and human detection. This robot was designed combination with Arduino Uno, a 15W UV lamp, ultrasonic sensors, PIR sensor, and EP32 Cam for disinfection and multitasking functions. Designing autonomous UV disinfection robots had been simulated and observed to test whether the UV robot model design can detect the obstacle and humans. The process of testing this UV robot model through simulation and hardware had been achieved. This robot can detect obstacles 15cm away and detect human presence.

articleTitle: Bibliometric Analysis of Conjugate Gradient Method and Image Processing Using Scopus Database
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Conjugate Gradient (CG) is the iterative method that is most prominent for solving systems of linear equations. This study aims to establish a practical single-source reference regarding CG and image processing. Utilizing the bibliometric approach in this study helps in identifying and evaluating the data in the 1974 CG and image processing-related materials. The data was extracted from a Scopus database and processed in Microsoft Excel. The VOSviewer program aids in displaying the data, while the Harzing Publish or Perish program aids in combining the data. The findings reveal that CG research began as early as 1977. Based on the statistics, the Measurement Science and Technology journal published the most publications on CG and image processing. However, there is limited research in this sector as proven by the top 20 cited publications list. Because this paper is limited to articles published in the Scopus database, the representativeness of ‘conjugate gradient and image’ research is deemed moderate. This bibliometric study could be utilized to supplement meta-analysis and organized literature reviews.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-Layered Wideband Wearable Monopole Antenna with Circular Parasitic Element for Breast Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: A dual-layered wideband antenna with coplanar waveguide (CPW)-base and circular parasitic element technique was proposed. In comparison to past research problems, which largely produced omnidirectional and hard antennas, it should be flexible, unidirectional, wideband, low weight, and compact. The wearable antenna consists of three stages, whereby Antenna <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> is designed by a basic rectangular antenna with CPW. Design <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex> is the next stage of antenna design development with the patch size modified. Antenna <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> is the next development stage with extra circular parasitic element and felt substrate. The bandwidth of 4.11 GHz (79.8 %) of the proposed antenna, which ranges from 2.89 GHz to 7.0 GHz, combines a number of wideband resonant frequencies, including those at 3.07 GHz, 3.90 GHz, 4.35 GHz, 5.15 GHz, and 6.32 GHz. There is also a 40 MHz-wide narrowband that functions between 1.15 GHz and 1.19 GHz and with resonance at 1.17 GHz. This proposed antenna is designed to develop a multifunction application future work system, particularly for breast cancer detection.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Based System on Enhancing the Capabilities of Transport System: A Systemic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Recent years have seen a considerable increase in the difficulty for our society in ensuring deep-rooted sustainability of traditional technology involve in critical structure. The role of Artificial intelligence (AI) is gaining importance significantly. By delivering ubiquitous real-time applications, It has aided in improving smart environments in many different industries, including smart cities, manufacturing, transportation, health, and the Internet of Things (IoT) by delivering ubiquitous real-time applications. As the technologies like natural language processing, deep learning, machine learning (ML), and others dramatically improve the functionality of communications, digital commerce, content, and apps, AI is poised to fundamentally change the information and communications technology (ICT) industry. Technological advancements brought changes that affect how we live nationally and internationally. The expansion of the economy has been significantly influenced by transportation. It has recently faced several challenges, including the competitiveness of public transportation and an inability to improve its services. Transport systems continue to have operational issues that deter people from using them. These include the fact that drivers frequently travel either deliberately, slowly, or dangerously quickly, making the schedules posted at bus stops untrustworthy. The most effective remedies to these cyber threats are developed using AI, which also offers the best answer. Security hazards are another unexpected effect of these technological improvements. In order to increase the effectiveness of transportation operations and improve public service, this study makes use of cutting-edge artificial intelligence technology. It also clarifies the capabilities of an AI-based transport system to guarantee high dependability and security in the future. The paper also discusses how AI-based systems can play a part in the intelligent transport system.

articleTitle: Teaching Assignment Based on NASH Equilibrium and Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Teaching assignment refers to the process of allocating classes to instructors for a given academic semester. Its outcome is a schedule that must adhere to various constraints, such as ensuring that all classes have assigned instructors, avoiding schedule conflicts among instructors, and adhering to predetermined limits on the number of classes assigned to each instructor. It is a complex task due to the involvement of multiple stakeholders such as instructors, and academic departments, each with their own interests. In many cases, these interests may conflict with each other. In this study, we propose using the NASH equilibrium, a branch of game theory, to analyze conflicts of interest among stakeholders and modeling the teaching assignment as a multi-objective optimization problem. Furthermore, we develop a genetic algorithm to solve this problem. Our algorithm is experimented with a real-world dataset consisting of 153 classes and 25 instructors. The experimental results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of our proposition.

articleTitle: Development of an IoT-Enabled Automated Marine Sand Washing Machine with Conductivity Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: This paper presents an automated marine sand washing system based on the conductivity measurement performed at various mix ratio of marine sand and harvested rain water. The amount of the chloride ion removed in marine sand will be reflected as a decrease in conductivity measurement. The proposed automated system will perform sand washing to reduce the amount of chloride ion in marine sand based on the conductivity measurement, which helps worker to monitor and deliver sand that meets the industry standards for construction purpose. Meanwhile, Volhard's chemical testing method was used to verify the amount of chloride ion in the sample sand compared with the conductivity measurement. Based on the experimental results, two linear regression models from different conductivity probes were proposed to predict chloride content in the sand. The programmable logic controller (PLC) was adopted to implement control logic of the automation process of the machine including watering, mixing, dewatering, and sand discharge. Furthermore, Internet of Things (IoT) was used to monitor the data received from various sensors and enable the user to remotely control the system. The results show that the proposed automated system is able to perform marine sand washing and the linear regression model can help in the estimating the required conductivity to meet the required standard of the chloride concentration in sand for construction purpose.

articleTitle: An University Student Dropout Detector Based on Academic Data
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Dropout at university has become a controversial problem in recent years, resulting in severe consequences for students and universities. Our research focuses on predicting early dropout to provide school administrators with warnings about at-risk students. This enables schools to offer appropriate solutions and support. This research explores the influence of academic performance on student dropout. We evaluated the proposed method on a dataset using comprehensive information about students, subjects, and academic performance. By extracting features and grouping them based on similar characteristics, we summarized critical information from the raw database. The problem is divided into two phases: English preparation terms and Main terms, aligning with the university's program structure. However, the data on dropout status is imbalanced, and numerous essential values are missing. To address this, we employed three deep learning models: the convolution-based model (CNN), the graph convolution network-based model (GCN), and the tabular learning model (TabNet). We compared the performance of these deep learning models with traditional machine learning algorithms: logistic regression (LR), support vector classifier (SVC), and light gradient boosting machine (LGBM) with feature selection. Our deep learning models outperformed tree-based algorithms, achieving a balanced accuracy of 72% in the English preparation phase and 75% in primary terms. It is worth noting that TabNet prioritizes recall at the expense of precision, while CNN and GCN models yield more balanced results.

articleTitle: Some Metaheuristics for Tourist Trip Design Problem
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Symposium on Industrial Electronics & Applications (ISIEA)
abstract: Tourist Trip Design Problem (TTDP) is fundamental in improving tourists' travel experiences and urban development. This study introduces a recommender engine to create a tour trip plan. The output of the system is a detailed trip itinerary for the tourist. It allows the tourist to determine the places to visit, the length of stay, and the entire route. The system's core is an optimizer for the combinatorial multi-objective optimization problem (MOP). There, users specify time and budget conditions as a query for the system. We have proposed a combination of Compromise Programming (CP) and Metaheuristics for this multi-objective optimization problem. Our method can handle situations where decision-makers cannot assign preferences to each goal and different decision-making scenarios. We have built two metaheuristic algorithms based on the proposed approach, which are Genetic Algorithm (GA) and another is Ant Colony Optimization (ACO). The objective was to examine how the influence of different search strategies affects the quality of the solution. The results show that ACO's swarm search strategy allows for finding slightly better-quality solutions than GA. However, it must trade-off with CPU time. We also compared the proposed method with the Posteriority approach to MOP. The results show that CP-based algorithms are superior to NSGA-II in finding a Pareto frontier.
